I am sincerely of the opinion that the minister would be well advised to hold up this legislation and not start another branch which to my mind is not necessary, and I say that after having listened with reasonable care to what the minister has said and to the discussion that has taken place.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
I have a purpose in rising
at this time, Mr. Chairman. I believe this change will make for efficiency. There seems to be more than one head to this body now; and I am sure the leader of the opposition, being a medical man of note, would agree that one head was enough for one body. We have reason to believe that the work of this branch is increasing, and it is most important work. We can send down to this branch, secure films and send them back to our constituencies without any charge of any kind. Many of these films were shown in Chippawa park last year, and they attracted and interested tourists from outside Canada.
I desired to ask whether the work of this department was growing rapidly, and also whether the department is now under one head? My other purpose was to tell the minister that one of the most important sections of Canada seems to have been left out when these films were made. Those who know the head of the lakes will agree that there we have scenery second to none on the continent of north America. For instance, we have Kakabeka Falls, with 190 foot head. If the minister will see that these pictures include some of the beautiful scenery at the head of the lakes, I am sure it will interest tourists from all over this and other countries.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
Mr. Chairman, I gather
that in connection with this bill the minister is permitting a general discussion of the whole situation, and I think we must look at it from the point of view of the importance of the job that is to be done. After all, we have at hand an organization for the production of films. As I understand it, the minister is not anxious to add to that organization; rather, he desires some body which through one individual, the commissioner, will have control over the production of films for the various departments of government. His idea, as I gather it, is not to add to the present film division; his desire is to have a coordinating body.
The success or failure of the coordinating body which he suggests, as I see it, depends upon two main factors. In the first place the success of what he has in mind will depend very largely upon the choice of the commissioner. If the commissioner is a man who has not had the full breadth of experience necessary for this position, he will not be of value to the board to which he is responsible; for, after all, he will be the connecting link between that board and the mechanical production of these films. Therefore he must be a technical man, able to give to the board such advice which is so necessary in the production of a successful film.
According to this bill, there are three gentlemen outside the permanent civil service who are to be appointed to the board. When discussing the resolution the other evening I suggested to the minister what I thought was a most important point. I suggested he make sure that among these three men there should be at least one-it would be preferable to have more-who had certain experience, not only in the production of film but in its conception. After all, an idea is one thing and the production of it is another. It is all very well for the minister of any department to suggest that a film should be produced to accomplish a certain purpose which he has in mind-it may be that the tourist bureau would want to show that in certain parts of Canada there are attractions for the tourists in the form of bass, maskalonge or otherwise- but one would not expect the minister to be a showman, as I suggested the other night. The conception of that film would be one thing; its production would be another. Just exactly how are you going to provide a short to be shown on the screens in the northern part of the United States drawing attention to the fact that there are certain areas in Canada where the maskalonge is just waiting for the tourist to come to take him home? After all, there are various ways in which that
National Film Board

can be done. I have seen it done successfully and I have seen it done badly. Therefore, in considering the suggestion which the minister makes, I think it is highly desirable that the commissioner should be the type of man which I have outlined. And further, as I have said, at least one and preferably two of the three men to be appointed outside the permanent civil service should be of the type who can give the fullest and best advice to the whole board.
I do not know whether the minister has anyone directly in mind to be appointed commissioner, but this man should possess three main attributes. In the first place, he should be a technical man or he should be constantly making contacts with those who have technical ability. He should be able to tell the board whether or not what is suggested is possible. After all, there may be a suggestion made in all sincerity by a minister for the production of a certain film which might present unusual and extraordinary technical difficulties. The commissioner ought to be able to see at once that while such a film can be produced, if it were produced in a certain way it could be turned out at perhaps a third of the cost. He should have some knowledge of the technical difficulties which may be encountered in the production of film and some realization of the technical possibilities.
Then he should be a showman in his own way. He should have some idea of how a film should register upon an audience. He should be able to say to a minister whether or not the suggested film will be suitable for the type of audience to which it is to be shown. In the third place, and probably the most important, he should be an advertising man. If we look through the pages of our newspapers, if we glance at our magazines or if we listen to our radio we do not find it difficult to tell whether the advertising we see or the advertising we hear has been prepared or produced by a man who knows something about that art. The effect of advertising, be it received through the eye or through the ear, or both simultaneously, must be spontaneous. To be effective, advertising must be at once effective. When you see a film, the impression which it is intended to leave is either left upon your mind or it is not. It seems to me that the necessity for an advertising type of commissioner is an exceedingly important point.
There is a great need for films to present Canada, not only to Canadians but to the people in other parts of the world. The minister knows from his own experience in other countries that the phrase "made in Canada ' does not have the effectiveness it
fMr. McIvor.J
should. We are proud of our agricultural products, as we have every right to be; we are confident that our manufactured products are of a type and kind which should have acceptance on the markets of the world. Certainly it is the policy of hon. gentlemen opposite that it is highly to be desired the channels of trade be opened to Canadian produce and to Canadian manufactured products. On the other hand, any salesman knows that adequate advertising decreases sales resistance and heightens desire, and thus is an important part of successful trade.
As the government of Canada has made it possible, through such agreements as the Ottawa agreements of 1932, to permit our entry into the market of the United Kingdom, it seems to me to be highly desirable, from the point of view of the producer of this country, that the government assume its share of responsibility in attempting to merchandise those products in that particular market. I have been to various shops, vegetable markets and so forth in the United Kingdom, and I have found great difficuty in obtaining made-in-Canada goods. I am sure the Minister of Trade and Commerce (Mr. Euler) and the Minister of Agriculture (Mr. Gardiner) will agree on at least this one point, that we should advertise our merchandise as fully as possible, be it agricultural products or be it manufactured products, in the market in which we are attempting to sell.
Canada is a tremendous country capable of producing highly diversified products, but I have yet to happen to be in an English or Scotch cinema when there was being shown a picture depicting Canada from the point of view of the production of farm products or the production of manufactured products. The average resident of the United Kingdom has little idea of the length and breadth of Canada; he has little idea of what our prairies look like and so on, but he can be shown these things. This need not be done according to the Hollywood conception; it need not be based upon some absurd drama; it should be by means of a carefully prepared government film. For example, if we are to sell our excellent prairie beef in the United Kingdom, surely the consumer in the United Kingdom should have an opportunity of seeing from what part of the world that beef comes. Such a film could be made extremely attractive.
Then I turn to the tourist trade. The average resident of the United Kingdom has never been to Canada. The number of tourists from the United Kingdom to Canada

National Film Board
is very small compared with the number that come from the United States. Perhaps this year the resident of the United Kingdom may be a little wary of going to the continent. He likes to travel, and he should be made to realize that Canada can provide a perfect and comparatively safe playground for his summer holiday. Are we in the process of preparing adequate advertising literature, films or whatever may be needed to attract the visitor to Canada? I am sure Mr. Dolan is to be heartily congratulated upon the work he has done with the tourist bureau; but, as I have said in the past in committee, the vote which we grant each year for the development of our tourist trade is highly inadequate. Our tourist trade has been one of our most profitable businesses. Many hundreds of thousands of tourists come here each year from the United States, but we can do more, much more, to develop this trade.
To sum up what I have said, it seems to me that the purpose of this bill is perfectly sound from many different points of view. I fully realize that there may be the danger of appointing another commission, that we may be providing a temptation to broaden out and spend more money. I suggest to the minister that he has at hand, without going very much further, the necessary material to build up through readjustment what he has essentially proposed in his bill. I have, as I have already said, great confidence in Mr. Badgley. It seems to me the work he has done so far has demonstrated that he possesses in great part those attributes I suggest the commissioner should possess. The minister may say that it is a two-man job to run a film bureau and to act as commissioner on this board. It may be so. On the other hand, if that is so, instead of retaining the present set-up of the film bureau why would it not be possible from out of the film bureau to take the head as a sort of commissioner and give him the necessary assistants to carry on the work which he would not be able to carry on by himself in the future as a result of his new responsibility. I think it is quite possible, Mr. Chairman, to form, as it were, a committee rather than a board within both the ministry and the permanent civil service.

Then I do not wish to detain the committee any longer. I have spoken at greater length than I had intended.
I just want to say in conclusion that I think the minister will find and appreciate that he has on hand at the moment the necessary machinery for the production of films, and that in his effort to coordinate the activities of the various departments he will arrive at the conclusion that a board composed of the present available personnel is the best possible means of achieving that end. I suggest that he give full consideration to the possibility of developing the board itself from within the ranks of those who sit on the treasury benches and of the permanent civil service, bearing in mind that he has at his disposal the services of two such able gentlemen as Mr. Badgley and Mr. Dolan.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION

speechtext: I am not sure that I can at the moment give the particular types of film distributed, although I can procure that for a later stage. The motion picture bureau has a world-wide circulation for its films far in excess of any other film organization in Canada and probably greater than any other governmental film organization in the world. It has more films in circulation in more countries than any other organization in Canada. The bureau has produced twenty-three new films in the last year. It has at the present time over 6,000 copies of its films in active circulation in about thirty countries and is reaching an estimated audience of probably 40,000,000 people each year. subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
Is not the story which the minister has just told of the very good distribution that is now taking place an argument against what he is proposing? In other words, the present distribution is so good, as he has just described it to us that I do not see why he needs any different type of organization. That struck me when the minister was giving his explanation. While I knew there was a considerable distribution. I do not mind saying I had no idea it was so widespread as the minister has just indicated. A distribution of film that reaches 40,000.000 people and spreads over thirty different countries seems to me a splendid distribution. The organization would seem to be doing such excellent work that I do not know why the minister wishes to change it. That is what puzzles me a bit. I think a little widening out along the line suggested by my hon. friend the member for Greenwood (Mr. Massey)-and that was really the suggestion which was made by the hon. member for Kootenay East and myself, namely that the present organization be widened-with Mr. Badgley remaining as the head, and something in the way of an interdepartmental committee to advise him, should answer the purpose. If the minister wished, there could also

be something in the way of outside honorary advisers. But the idea of bringing in another commissioner, and setting up another bureau over Mr. Badgley and the men who have brought about this splendid distribution, seems unnecessary and really strange to me.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
I am sure that my hon.
friend will agree that nothing is ever so good that it cannot be improved, and that is exactly what we hope to do in the setting up of this organization. Something has been said with regard to Mr. Badgley who -is now director of the bureau, and the suggestion has been made that he could handle the whole thing. I have nothing to say of Mr. Badgley but what is good; he is an excellent official. But- and when I say this I am giving no intimation whether Mr. Badgley or anyone else is to be the commissioner because neither the government nor I have given any consideration to who the commissioner might be-I do contend that if we are going to carry on this work in the way that has been suggested by the hon. member for Greenwood and according to what is in my own mind, it means a better distribution, the elimination of overlapping, and the creation of what we might call departmental films. I think there is a job there for two good men; one as a director of the bureau, to do the work that is being done now-and perhaps still better work is possible with added facilities-and certainly there some one else is needed for the framing of national policies and the producing of national pictures such as will be done by the board with the assistance of the commissioner, the commissioner being an executive officer.
I am convinced, after giving this matter a great deal of thought, that it will add to the efficiency of our picture distribution if we adopt a plan something of this kind. The bureau itself is the productive factor. The work of initiating films, especially of a national character, is something entirely different. It is related to it; but it requires, to my mind, a different kind of efficiency-initiative, and the power of developing films on a national basis for educative purposes, advertising purposes and so forth. Not the production itself, which is more or less a mechanical job, but the initiating of ideas in connection with national films, requires something more in the way of special capacity, and it is for that reason we want to enlist the services of someone from the outside.
The hon. member for Greenwood made a very good point, I thought, when he said that there will be required on that board one technical man who knows something of the

National Film Board
film business, something of the value of advertising, something of the sort of appeal which can be made to the public. That knowledge ought also to be in the commissioner himself, and it is going to be an important matter to select the right man for that position. It may be Mr. Badgley; I do not knowT. There seems to be considerable solicitude in the committee as to what will become of Mr. Badgley. I am not prepared to say. I am perfectly sincere when I say that the selection of the commissioner has not been made even tentatively as far as I am concerned. But I believe that if we want to carry out the principles outlined in the bill, to coordinate the work of the various departments and initiate national films for general country-wide educational purposes, we need the two organizations and their officers, the director of the bureau and the commissioner to proceed with the work under the board itself.
I do not know that I can make any better argument. I could give, perhaps in more detail, a description of the work it is hoped to do. I could give a description of the work which is now being done, and show that the work done by the various departments individually and separately, while good in itself, can be tremendously improved by eliminating some of the overlapping and unnecessary expenditure.
I should like again to reassure if I can some hon. members who seem to fear that we are going to set up a costly organization to run into hundreds of thousands of dollars of expenditure and create another bureaucracy. I regard that as imaginary. I do not believe it will happen, because the committee should remember that all the moneys the board will spend must be voted by this parliament. On the board there will be two members of the government and three civil servants. From that it surely must be evident that the operations will be thoroughly under the control of the government itself and of parliament. So long as I happen to be at the head of the department there is not going to be any spreading out of an expensive staff in connection with this board. As a matter of fact, I am astonished that so much argument has arisen in connection with it. It is not a tremendously expensive agency that we propose to set up; it is just something which seems to me to be the sensible and businesslike thing to do. So far from creating expense, I believe we shall eliminate some expense and obtain more efficiency than we have had hitherto. That is all the purpose we have in mind.

You could make your committee of one or two ministers plus several senior civil servants, and establish it by an administrative act without any legislation at all, under the precedent I have already cited.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: My hon. friend was minister of this department and therefore was chairman of the committee of ministers which had to do with the research council.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Yes.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
Did he find any difficulty
in getting these ministers together and getting any actual service out of them? I did.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: No. I had associated with me Doctor MacLaren, Doctor Sutherland and Mr. Gordon, and I have forgotten whom ' else. I think there were five ministers. I had no difficulty. I simply sent a notice out and they met in my office quite frequently.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: The hon. member's experience is better than mine.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
That may be. But we
had no difficulty. The committee functioned admirably.
There is another point which, at least in my view, should be cleared up. The minister has referred several times to the bureau as "technical." Certainly the bureau is technical, but I want to tell him and tell this committee that the bureau under its present direction has all the elements of vision which are necessary for the production and designing of films. I was amazed at the unusual skill which was present there for the designing and production of film subjects. All we have to do is go over the library of films. If hon. members are interested they could go to the bureau and have a few of them put on the screen. It might be a good idea for the minister to invite members to go to the bureau to see those films, because I believe they are excellent. The hon. member for Greenwood stated a minute ago that he has not seen any in the old country. I was in the old country and I saw a number of them.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
I said I happened not to
have seen them.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
I remember seeing a
number of excellent films. I saw some Russian films, and films from other countries exhibited at the same time. I would say that those from Canada were in every respect fMr. Stevens.]
equal to those from other countries. We have no reason, with our present organization -its efficiency, its skill, its science and its art-to take a back seat to any of them. It must not be permitted to go on the basis that, as we now have the technical requirements, we must set up a board and a commissioner to put into it the brains-or the science, or art, as the case may be-because we have that now.
I question very much whether, under the present scheme, we shall improve that phase of it one iota. I should like to see a committee of council, with the minister as chairman and with two or three other ministers associated with him who would have definite administrative instructions from the government. It would have to be one central film operation, and it would stop all this nonsense where individual departments may go off and buy films from the outside. The minister said a moment ago he was not quite sure, but I venture to say to him that every dollar of that $50,000 was spent outside the government service. I will venture to say further-and I challenge contradiction-that in addition to that it will be found there are little, miniature organizations in two or three other departments, organizations of semiskilled individuals who call themselves film experts, carrying on a sort of secondary or subsidiary film bureau in the different departments. All that is required is a bit of administrative action on the part of the government to stop this useless duplication and this senseless broadening out of these things, after this first coordination was effected some years ago. There is now a coordinated body. Instead of erecting a new coordination organization, the government should take a step backward and insist that the department observe the present arrangement, respect it, and call for their service through that body.
With all due regard to the minister and his intentions-which I believe are serious; he knows very well I am not reflecting upon him in any personal way-I warn him, I warn the government and I warn the committee that if we go ahead with this organization we are simply going to- superimpose on an existing excellent organization another one which will ultimately become very costly.
Let us turn to the next clause, which has already been discussed to some extent, and just visualize what it means. The minister is providing for a board to hold office for three years, one to retire each year for the first three years, and from then on they will hold office for three years-all outside members, as well as members of the privy council and the civil service. Once a board of

National Film Board
that kind, on which are outside persons appointed for terms of three years, is erected, they will start building up a little bureaucracy within the government; whereas, if a committee of council is appointed under the present authority, with no further legislation we would keep the administration under the control of the minister in charge.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: It will be that way, because the minister will be the chairman; one colleague will sit with him, and three civil servants.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: But you are erecting a board with outsiders on it. You can always call in an expert from any part of the country, and pay him for whatever advice you get. But in this way you are erecting a bureaucracy within the department, instead of maintaining ministerial control, which the hon. member for Temiscouata dilated upon so eloquently on Friday night.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
There is a new and improved educational development in Alberta under the supervision of the minister of education. It has been declared by the minister in that province that they intend to a greater extent to U9e films throughout the schools of the province. Many of the schools, as well as churches and other institutions throughout Alberta, have facilities to make available to the public whatever national films may be produced by the department.
I find myself in accord with the bill. I should like to learn from the minister how many educational films we have which could be supplied to the schools.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: I am afraid I cannot give the number now, but I could get the information for the hon. member. I should not like to give a definite figure.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: What steps are being taken to inform the schools and churches as to the type and number of films they may have?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: They merely have the knowledge that these films are in existence at the bureau, and when they write in for them the films are sent. I do not know that there is anything further done in connection with the matter.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: The explanatory note refers to the government film distribution and public information service. I understand this is already provided.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: What is the question?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
The note says:
Its main concern will be the organization of a central government film distribution and public information service.
As I understand it, we already have the public information service, and this will effect no improvement.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: It will just have the effect of intensifying the work now being done. I see my hon. friend the former minister has left the chamber, and what I am about to say is not said with the intention of criticizing, but I believe I could point out that in the past the work of distribution and production has been more or less haphazard. It is our desire to unify it and make it better than it was before.

Section agreed to.
On section 3-National Film Board.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Is there any theory of cooperation between the national board and the various boards in the provinces?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: There are not any provincial boards.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Did not some of the provinces have their own motion picture bureaux?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Not now.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: None of them?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: None at all. Ontario did have one, but it has been discontinued.

Section agreed to.
Sections 4 to 7 inclusive agreed to.
On section 8-Government film commissioner.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Is there any intention of broadening out the duties of the government film commission in such a way as to effect or to have any influence upon anything connected with outside work, or films outside the government; or is this entirely for the purpose of broadening out the work presently done by the government?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Entirely government work.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: If this added expense is to be incurred, will the outside purchasing of films, which apparently has been going on, be discontinued?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
It all depends. If some department can convince the film board that its work could be better done by some outside organization it will be done, but it must first get the consent of the board.
National Film Board

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: In connection with the visit of their majesties to Canada there will, of course, be moving pictures taken for the archives and as a matter of record. Would this department handle that?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: All arrangements in connection with the royal visit are being handled by a government committee. I have no doubt the bureau will do some of the work; at least I hope so. Whether it will be confined to the bureau, I cannot say.

Section agreed to.
On section 9-Duties of commissioner.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
Would the minister be
willing to add as the first clause of paragraph 9 something like the following:
advise upon the making and distribution of national films designed to help Canadians in all parts of Canada to understand the ways of living and the problems of Canadians in other parts.
The minister used the words earlier this evening, but as I read the bill there is no mention in it of national films. Yet the vision of what national films can mean seems to me the most important feature about this bill. I agree with the minister that national films could mean a great deal in building up the Canadian nation.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: I think my hon. friend will find in the bill the term "national films."

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: It is in paragraph (a).

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
Yes, "coordinate national
and departmental film activities." I assure my hon. friend it is the intention of the government that national films shall be initiated.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: For the sake of the people who are administering this act in the future, it would be well to set that out clearly in this section. After all, the important idea behind this bill is that there should be national films developed, and I think that should be stressed more than it is in the bill as drawn.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: If my hon. friend thinks that the phrase "coordinate national film activities" is not sufficient, we might say "coordinate and originate" or "coordinate and develop national film activities."

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: I think that feature is worthy of a separate clause. I have one here that I shall send over to the minister.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
Does the government at present do all its own film work?
	{

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: No; that is one of the reasons for this bill; some of the departments are having their film work done outside, and some may continue to do so; but it is hoped that, having a bureau that is as good as the best, the various departments will have their work done by this bureau; in fact they must, unless the board agrees to its being done otherwise.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
The other night
when we were discussing this matter I asked the minister if it was the intention of the department to put this film business on a more or less commercial basis. No doubt there will be commercial firms who would like to have these pictures taken and shown in various countries. Could not the government get some revenue out of this bureau?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: I am afraid I cannot give my hon. friend any greater encouragement than I did the other evening. This is advertising, not a money-making concern. I have not a great deal of hope that when we supply these short films to theatres and other places we can collect much revenue for them. I am told that the British government issues some films out of which it makes a little money, but I should not like to say that we are going to make much out of this. We are running it for the purpose of doing our own advertising. If we can make a little profit it will be that much to the good, but I should not like to give much hope of making money out of the film bureau. We do not hope to make money out of supplying films to schools and institutions of that sort.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
It seems to me
there could be a source of revenue. We have our trade commissioners throughout the world looking for trade, and our manufacturers of one kind and another who are looking for business. I think it would be easy to develop a great source of revenue in connection with this bureau. If we start out on the basis that we are not going to make anything out of it, we certainly shall not. But I think the government should see that we do have one section of it that will handle this film business from the point of view of advertising Canadian products, and I think the various manufacturers in this country would be quite willing to pay for that service. At the present time they pay for the sendee they get from the national research council. As we all know, that council has developed into a profitable institution; at least it pays its way, and there is no reason why this bureau should not be put on the same basis.

National Film Board

speechtext:
I move
the amendment suggested by the hon. member for Vancouver South (Mr. Green):
That section 9 be amended by inserting the following as subsection (a):
advise upon the making and distribution of national films designed to help Canadians in all parts of Canada to understand the ways of living and the problems of Canadians in other parts. .

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: In regard to expenditures by the various departments, might I ask the minister if there is any provision in this bill that would compel the other departments to have their films produced by this branch?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Section 11 deals with that.

Section agreed to.
On section 10-Departments to refer matters to commissioner.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Does not subsection 2 presuppose that the departments are going to endeavour to invest in apparatus themselves; and is that not contrary to the explanation the minister gave, that it was the hope of the government that the work of the department could be concentrated in this bureau?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: According to a note I have here, it is estimated that the value of camera, projection and film servicing equipment at present in possession of all departments-that is, other than the motion picture bureau-is about 825,000, which has been purchased piecemeal from different sources. This equipment is not standardized to any extent, and in some instances is not the most suitable equipment for the purpose for which it was purchased. It is not intended, of course, that any department is to take the place of the bureau, but it may be that small purchases will have to be made, and that will be done under the supervision of the director.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: So the various departments still will be permitted to maintain their own apparatus and make their own films?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: They cannot do it without the consent of the director.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Who purchases the equipment provided for in subsection 3?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
The body which has an
appropriation for the purpose, but it must be all under the supervision of the director.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Any department?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Yes.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: If the purchase of apparatus is to be made only with the consent of the board, I do not see anything in the bill which would similarly prevent any department from making its own pictures with such apparatus as it has now. It is not incumbent upon the department to turn over its apparatus to the motion picture bureau, so it can continue its own little parasitical bureau.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Yes, but it cannot produce any films. Section 11 provides that all processing and production of films must be undertaken by the bureau, except where the commissioner agrees that the work can be done through officers of other departments. They cannot make their own films without the consent of the commissioner.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: But on the other hand the departments now have a certain amount of apparatus of their own, and the temptation will be for the departments to continue the work they are now doing. They may be able to prevail upon the commissioner to give them permission to do so. Why not have the departments turn over all apparatus to the bureau?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: That is probably what will happen. The possibility of any department going on with the production of its own films is rather remote, in view of the bill now being considered. They cannot do very much in the production of real films in any event. In the past they have either used the equipment of the bureau or had the work done by an outside firm. They can no longer do that without the consent of the board and the commissioner.

Section agreed to.
Section 11 agreed to.
On section 12-Employment of temporary staff.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Is there any good reason why we should not allow these appointments to be made under the civil service commission?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
For the simple reason that in many instances, perhaps when certain films are being made, a great deal of temporary help will be required, perhaps specially qualified help. It would take too long to have these appointments made by the civil service commission; and I think perhaps it is no insult to the commission to say that possibly the officer of the board would be much better qualified to select these technical temporary employees than would the civil service commission. In point of the time

National Film Board

required, particularly, it would be quite out of place to utilize the services of the civil service commission.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Then what procedure will be followed in engaging temporary personnel?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: The director of the bureau may employ temporary help.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Would it not be possible, in anticipation of a demand of that kind, to have an eligible list established by the civil service commission from which the director could draw from time to time? We pass act after act in this house containing the expression "notwithstanding anything in the Civil Service Act," and at the same time the government has declared itself as being in favour of the merit system.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: What my hon. friend says is true in a general way. But supposing the bureau has to produce a particularly important film, or a film of such a character that it became necessary to bring somebody even from Hollywood; I do not think anyone would expect the director to go to the civil service commission to obtain a person of that sort. This has to do with men of technical qualifications, engaged for very short periods.

Section agreed to.
Section 13 agreed to.
On section 14-Central government film distribution service.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Would the minister explain to the committee what government film distribution service there is at the present time? Is this in addition, or is there any change?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: It is really just an expansion of the present service. The bureau-is distributing films now, and it is perhaps to make it just a little more official. Assistance will be given by this departmental committee which is to be set up, and this is more or less to give it official standing.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: To incorporate it in the act?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Yes.

Bill reported.

To-morrow we shall take up the second reading of Bill No. 38, to establish a defence purchasing board, standing in the name of the Minister of National Defence (Mr. [\Ir. Euler.]
Mackenzie); and also, in committee of ways and means, the trade agreement, as well as any other bill standing on the order paper if we dispose of those items.

About ten days ago, I
think, or perhaps a littler longer, I mentioned in the house that one of our members was going to move an amendment on going into supply. There has been no motion for some time to go into supply and, if possible, we should like to have that motion to-morrow. If we cannot have it to-morrow, possibly it could be done on Wednesday, but there is no motion for committee of supply on Thursday and Friday. In justice to hon. members I think the government should move to go into supply on such days as Monday or Tuesday, because that is the one opportunity when hon. members may deal with important subjects not on the order paper. If possible, I should like the minister to consider this matter. So far as I am concerned, he can advise me in the morning whether the government considers it possible to move to go into supply to-morrow in order to give an opportunity to one of our members to move an amendment, notice of which I gave from my place in the house I think ten or twelve days ago.

I shall bring that suggestion to the attention of the Prime Minister (Mr. Mackenzie King). I think the purpose is to move along with the bills under consideration in order to get them finished so that they may be sent across to the other house. In any event, I assume we would be moving to go into supply not later than Monday of next week. While the urgency of the matter suggested by the leader of the opposition (Mr. Manion) may be considerable, it probably could stand until the beginning of next week. However, I shall bring this to the attention of the Prime Minister in the morning and ask his office to advise the leader of the opposition.
